hero.title: Disaster Fund
hero.description: How much Aparri set aside each year for disasters, and how much of it was spent.

content.intro: By law (Republic Act 10121), every town must set aside at least 5% of its regular income as a Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). Most of it (70%) is for preparing for and reducing the impact of disasters. The rest (30%) is a Quick Response Fund kept ready for relief and recovery when a disaster strikes.

terms.description: The Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund: money the town must set aside each year for disasters, at least 5% of its regular income.
For training, equipment, early warning systems, drills and other work that reduces disaster risks before they happen.
Kept ready for relief and recovery when a disaster or calamity happens.
How much of the money set aside for the year was actually spent that year. Unspent money is not lost: the law keeps it in a trust fund for disaster use in the next five years.

content.sourceNote: Figures are from the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) annual "LDRRMF by LGU" files. FY 2025 figures are preliminary and may change. Per-resident amounts use mid-year population estimates between the 2015, 2020 and 2024 census counts.
